title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 04
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The back EMF in a DC motor opposes:
questions.solution: Back EMF opposes the armature current, limiting it to (V − Eb)/Ra.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The commutating poles (interpoles) carry current from:
questions.solution: Interpoles are connected in series with armature, carrying full armature current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In a DC compound motor, the series field is connected:
questions.solution: Series field winding is connected in series with the armature.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The efficiency of a DC motor at light load is:
questions.solution: At light load, fixed losses (iron + friction) dominate, reducing efficiency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The condition for maximum efficiency in a DC motor is:
questions.solution: Variable losses (copper) = Constant losses (iron + friction) at max efficiency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Sparking at the commutator is primarily due to:
questions.solution: Armature reaction distorts flux in neutral zone, causing delayed commutation and sparking.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The equalizer rings in a DC generator are used to:
options: Equalize current in parallel armature paths
questions.solution: Equalizer rings connect corresponding points of parallel armature paths to equalize circulating currents.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Lap winding in a DC machine is used for:
questions.solution: Lap winding has more parallel paths (A = P), suitable for low voltage, high current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Wave winding in a DC machine is used for:
questions.solution: Wave winding has 2 parallel paths, suitable for high voltage, low current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A DC motor's torque-speed characteristic in shunt configuration is:
questions.solution: Shunt motor has slightly drooping speed characteristic with load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The speed regulation of a DC shunt motor is typically:
questions.solution: DC shunt motor has good speed regulation (10–15% drop from no-load to full-load).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The braking torque in regenerative braking is limited by:
questions.solution: Back EMF cannot exceed supply voltage significantly, limiting regenerative braking torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A Ward-Leonard speed control system uses:
questions.solution: Ward-Leonard uses a DC generator driven by AC motor to supply variable DC voltage to DC motor armature.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In a DC series motor, the torque is proportional to armature current squared when:
questions.solution: When unsaturated, Φ ∝ Ia, so T ∝ ΦIa ∝ Ia².

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The type of starter used for a DC series motor is:
questions.solution: Series motor requires a 2-point starter because the holding coil is in series with the field.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The 4-point starter differs from 3-point starter in that:
options: Holding coil is connected across supply, not field
It is used for series motors only
questions.solution: In 4-point starter, no-volt coil is connected across supply through a separate resistance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The braking torque in plugging is higher than dynamic braking because:
options: Both supply and back EMF oppose rotation
questions.solution: In plugging, supply voltage reverses and adds to back EMF, creating high braking current/torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The armature current in a DC motor at starting is limited by:
questions.solution: At start, Eb = 0, so starter resistance limits starting current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If the field winding of a DC shunt motor is open-circuited while running:
questions.solution: No flux → no torque at finite speed, but residual flux causes speed to increase uncontrollably.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The hum in a transformer is caused by:
questions.solution: Magnetostriction causes core laminations to vibrate at twice supply frequency.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Which DC motor is used in elevators?
questions.solution: Cumulative compound motor provides high starting torque and good speed regulation for elevators.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The synchronous speed of an induction motor is given by:
questions.solution: Ns = 120f/P where f is supply frequency and P is number of poles.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The slip of an induction motor is defined as:
questions.solution: Slip s = (Ns − Nr)/Ns, where Nr is rotor speed.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: At standstill (locked rotor), the slip of an induction motor is:
questions.solution: At standstill, Nr = 0, so s = (Ns − 0)/Ns = 1.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotor frequency of an induction motor is:
questions.solution: Rotor frequency fr = s × f, where s is slip.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotating magnetic field in an induction motor is produced by:
questions.solution: Stator windings fed with 3-phase supply produce rotating magnetic field.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The direction of rotating magnetic field can be reversed by:
questions.solution: Reversing any two phases reverses the direction of rotating field.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The torque-slip characteristic of an induction motor shows:
options: Maximum torque at a specific slip
questions.solution: Torque increases with slip up to maximum (breakdown) torque, then decreases.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The starting torque of a squirrel cage induction motor is typically:
questions.solution: DOL starting torque is typically 1.5–2 times full load torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The star-delta starter reduces starting current by:
questions.solution: In star, line voltage is reduced by 1/√3, so current is reduced by 1/3 compared to delta.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An autotransformer starter reduces starting voltage, and starting current reduces by:
questions.solution: Starting current is proportional to k (autotransformer ratio), so it reduces by k² compared to DOL.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) controls induction motor speed by:
questions.solution: V/f control maintains constant flux by varying both V and f proportionally.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Crawling in an induction motor is caused by:
options: Space harmonics in air gap flux
questions.solution: Harmonics (5th, 7th) create parasitic torques causing motor to run at sub-synchronous speed.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Cogging (magnetic locking) in an induction motor occurs when:
options: Number of stator slots equals number of rotor slots
questions.solution: When stator and rotor slot numbers are equal or have common factor, magnetic locking prevents starting.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The double cage induction motor has:
options: Two cages with different resistance and reactance
questions.solution: Outer cage has high resistance (high starting torque), inner cage has low resistance (high efficiency).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Plugging in an induction motor involves:
options: Reversing any two stator phases while running
questions.solution: Reversing two phases reverses rotating field, creating braking torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotor resistance starting method is applicable to:
questions.solution: External resistance is added to rotor circuit through slip rings.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum torque of an induction motor is independent of:
questions.solution: Maximum torque depends on V, X2, and stator impedance but not on R2.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The pull-out (breakdown) torque of a standard induction motor is typically:
questions.solution: Breakdown torque is typically 2–3 times full load torque for standard motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The no-load current of an induction motor is typically what percentage of rated current?
questions.solution: No-load current is high (30–40%) because of magnetizing requirement of air gap.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The power factor of an induction motor at no load is:
questions.solution: At no load, current is mostly magnetizing (reactive), so power factor is low.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The air gap in an induction motor is kept small to:
questions.solution: Small air gap reduces reluctance, reducing magnetizing current and improving power factor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotor bars of a squirrel cage motor are made of:
questions.solution: Rotor bars are typically copper or aluminum (die-cast) for good conductivity.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The skewed rotor slots in an induction motor help to:
questions.solution: Skewing reduces harmonics, noise, cogging, and provides smoother torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An induction motor operates on the principle of:
questions.solution: Rotating stator field induces EMF in rotor by electromagnetic induction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The slip at maximum torque for a squirrel cage motor is typically:
questions.solution: Slip at maximum torque is around 0.1–0.2 for standard motors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The speed of an induction motor can be controlled by:
questions.solution: All methods are used: V/f control, rotor resistance, pole changing, and rotor voltage control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Pole changing (Dahlander) method gives speed ratio of:
questions.solution: Dahlander connection gives two speeds in ratio 1:2 (e.g., 4-pole and 8-pole).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The equivalent circuit of an induction motor at standstill is similar to:
questions.solution: At standstill, rotor frequency equals stator frequency, making it equivalent to a transformer with short-circuited secondary.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The magnetizing branch in an induction motor equivalent circuit represents:
questions.solution: Magnetizing branch (Rc || Xm) represents air gap flux and core losses.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The rotor copper loss in an induction motor is:
questions.solution: Rotor copper loss = s × Pag (air gap power).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The mechanical power developed in an induction motor is:
questions.solution: Pmech = (1−s) × Pag.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If the supply voltage of an induction motor is reduced by half, the torque:
questions.solution: Torque ∝ V², so halving voltage reduces torque to one-fourth.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The locked rotor test on an induction motor is similar to:
questions.solution: Locked rotor test gives parameters of equivalent circuit, similar to SC test on transformer.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The no-load test on an induction motor is similar to:
questions.solution: No-load test gives core loss and magnetizing branch parameters.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The circle diagram of an induction motor is drawn from:
questions.solution: Circle diagram is constructed from no-load and blocked rotor test data.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The V/f control of induction motor maintains:
questions.solution: V/f ratio is kept constant to maintain constant air gap flux (avoiding saturation).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: At very high frequencies, the V/f control of induction motor is limited by:
questions.solution: At high speeds, V cannot increase further due to supply/insulation voltage limit.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In field weakening mode of an induction motor (above base speed):
questions.solution: Above base speed, V is held constant while f increases, causing flux to reduce.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The skin effect in induction motor rotor bars causes:
questions.solution: At starting (high rotor frequency), skin effect increases effective rotor resistance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The bar-end ring in a squirrel cage motor connects:
questions.solution: End rings short-circuit all rotor bars at both ends of the rotor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The slip ring in an induction motor is used to:
questions.solution: Slip rings allow external resistance to be added to rotor circuit for starting/control.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The air gap power in an induction motor is the power:
options: Transferred across air gap from stator to rotor
questions.solution: Air gap power is the power crossing the air gap from stator to rotor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The efficiency of a standard induction motor at full load is typically:
questions.solution: Modern induction motors achieve 85–95% efficiency at full load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The power flow in an induction motor is:
options: Input → Stator loss → Air gap → Rotor loss → Mechanical output
Input → Rotor → Air gap → Stator → Output
questions.solution: Power flows: Pin → Stator copper/core loss → Pag → Rotor copper loss → Pmech − windage/friction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The torque developed by an induction motor is proportional to:
questions.solution: T ∝ Φ × I2 × cos(φ2), where Φ is air gap flux and I2 is rotor current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In an induction motor, the power factor can be improved by:
questions.solution: Power factor capacitors and reduced air gap (lower magnetizing current) both improve PF.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The blocked rotor test on an induction motor is conducted at:
questions.solution: Reduced voltage is applied to circulate rated current without overheating.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The torque equation of a 3-phase induction motor is:
questions.solution: Full torque equation considering slip, rotor resistance, and leakage reactance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The condition for maximum torque in an induction motor is:
questions.solution: Maximum torque occurs when R2 = sX2, i.e., slip at maximum torque sm = R2/X2.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In an induction motor, if rotor resistance is doubled, the slip at maximum torque:
questions.solution: sm = R2/X2, so doubling R2 doubles the slip at maximum torque.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The magnetizing current in an induction motor is higher than in a transformer because:
questions.solution: Air gap increases reluctance, requiring more magnetizing current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous motor runs at:
questions.solution: Synchronous motor always runs at synchronous speed regardless of load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous motor is not self-starting because:
options: Average torque on rotor is zero with rotating field
questions.solution: Rotor inertia prevents it from catching synchronous speed of rotating field.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: V-curves of a synchronous motor show the relationship between:
questions.solution: V-curves plot armature current vs. field excitation at constant load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: At normal excitation of a synchronous motor, the power factor is:
questions.solution: At normal excitation, synchronous motor operates at unity power factor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An over-excited synchronous motor operates at:
questions.solution: Over-excited synchronous motor draws leading current (acts like a capacitor).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An under-excited synchronous motor operates at:
questions.solution: Under-excited motor draws lagging current (like an inductor).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A synchronous condenser is:
options: A synchronous motor running at no load, over-excited
questions.solution: Synchronous condenser is an over-excited synchronous motor used for power factor correction.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Hunting in a synchronous motor is:
options: Oscillation of rotor about synchronous speed
questions.solution: Hunting is periodic oscillation of rotor due to sudden load changes.
